:::{#def-density-measure}
#### Density with respect to a measure, Radon--Nikodym derivative

<!-- check-definition-expectation: allow -->
<!-- The integral is the density's own defining property, Pr(X in A), not a probability-weighted average of another function, so no expectation fits. -->

Let $\measure$ be a [measure](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/measures-measure-spaces.html#def-measure)
on the [range of a random variable](#def-range) $X$, written $\rangef{X}$.
A **density with respect to a measure** $\measure$,
or **Radon--Nikodym derivative**,
of the [distribution](#def-cdf) of $X$
is a non-negative [measurable function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/measures-integrals.html#def-measurable-function) $f$ on $\rangef{X}$
whose [Lebesgue integral](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/measures-integrals.html#def-integral) against $\measure$,
not its [Riemann integral](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/calculus-integration.html#def-riemann-integral),
over each [measurable set](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/measures-measure-spaces.html#def-measurable-set) $A \subseteq \rangef{X}$
is the [probability](probability-basics.qmd#def-probability) that $X$ falls in $A$
[@billingsley1995probability, pp. 213, 423]:

$$\Pr(X \in A) = \int_A f(x)\,d\measure(x)$$

:::
